stem.en: According to the book, why was it so important to Egyptians to preserve a body?

text.en: They believed the ka, a spiritual double, lived on only if the body was preserved.
They wanted to stop diseases from spreading to the living.

feedback.en: The book gives a belief as the reason, not health. Burying a body would stop disease without any embalming.

text.en: Only pharaohs had souls, so only their bodies mattered.

feedback.en: The book says each person had a ka, not only the pharaoh.

text.en: Families wanted to be able to visit and see the dead.

feedback.en: Bodies were wrapped, placed in coffins and buried, so nobody was meant to see them again.

explanation.en: Egyptians believed each person had a ka that lived on after death if the body was preserved, so mummification was a way of caring for the dead.
